To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we did not observe a magnetic orientation in cattle and that we found no evidence for the existence of such a magnetic orientation in non-hominid, non-homing terrestrial mammals in general.
the experimental approach in our research did not support the hypothesis of a south-north orientation of cattle.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic field is not a reliable directional cue for these mammals, but that the sun direction may be.
the magnetic field is not involved in the orientation behavior of non-homing, large, non-migratory mammals.
the observed south-north alignment of resting non-homing, terrestrial, mammals is not a magnetic phenomenon, but is likely to result from a combination of other factors.
